questions.question: What does the idiom "it's raining cats and dogs" mean?
options: It is raining very heavily
Animals are falling from the sky
The weather is changing quickly
It is barely drizzling
questions.explanation: Idioms have figurative meanings — this one simply means it is raining very heavily.

questions.question: What is a phrasal verb?
options: A verb combined with a particle that creates a new meaning, like "give up"
A verb with more than three syllables
A verb used only in formal writing
A verb that cannot take an object
questions.explanation: Phrasal verbs combine a verb with a preposition or adverb (give up, look after) and often mean something different from the base verb.

questions.question: Why is it important to know WHEN to use informal language?
options: Using slang in the wrong context, like an exam essay, creates a poor impression
Informal language is always wrong
Formal language is forbidden among friends
Idioms only exist in informal English
questions.explanation: Informal language has rules of its own: knowing when it is appropriate matters as much as knowing what it means.

questions.question: What is the difference between slang and colloquial language?
options: Slang is very informal and group-specific; colloquial language is everyday informal speech used more widely
They are exactly the same
Colloquial language is used only by teenagers
Slang is always offensive
questions.explanation: Slang belongs to specific groups and changes fast, while colloquial language is general informal everyday speech.

questions.question: Why should you learn idioms even if you avoid using them in formal writing?
options: Native speakers use them constantly, so they are essential for understanding
They are required in every exam answer
They replace the need for grammar
They are easier than regular vocabulary
questions.explanation: Idioms appear constantly in conversation, media and literature — understanding them is essential for comprehension.
